rows.what the ink shows: A rounded left remnant and a tall terminal stroke survive two heavy horizontal cancellation strokes. The middle letter bodies and any i dot are merged with the cancellation, so the entire word cannot be established as soit.

Between the plus and the opening absolute-value bar is a dense rounded/angular ink mass with a short descending component and a rightward horizontal stroke. The canceled and surviving layers do not separate into an independently readable original r.

A detached broad upper stroke lies above a very compact low connected body with several small rises. Although the upper stroke is compatible with a circumflex, the body does not independently separate all four letters m/ê/m/e, and the shorter en reading cannot be excluded securely.

Above the surviving fraction bar an arched n and a separate factorial stroke with dot remain legible; the denominator's terminal factorial stroke and dot also survive. Broad diagonal and horizontal cancellations conceal the interior denominator and its parentheses, leaving the original denominator sequence uncertain.

The raised canceled factor shows a leading descending stem, a detached low dot and a heavily overstruck terminal loop/stem. These remnants favor the short factor visually, but they do not securely establish every glyph or the extent of the canceled expression; the whole original uncertainty is retained.

The subscript is a low rounded arch with a raised left approach and a downturned right end, matching the compressed n under the leftmost alpha on this same line. The nearby p in the next alpha's n-p index has a distinct extended descending stem and loop that are absent here.

An elongated looped capital P is followed by a short r, rounded o, low u trace and compact v body. The remaining dotlike/low sequence ends in a long rise and downward hook, but does not independently distinguish the complete ons ending from er.

After the canceled tout, the baseline letter has two connected shoulders with three descending turns, followed by a separate comma. Its double-shouldered shape agrees with the m product limits directly below and distinguishes it from the single arch of n.

The baseline cancellation has a long curved stroke crossing several short protrusions and terminating in a large descending flourish. The higher rewritten letter is a separate layer; the canceled baseline does not expose a complete m or securely delimit its original extent.

A complete small supralinear glyph sits above the long crossing of the earlier baseline writing: its left down/up cup is followed by a second shoulder and falling right leg, giving m. Its strokes remain separate from the canceled writing below.

The crossed display retains an S with upper m and lower n, parentheses around u+v, and a sum with upper m; the lower annotation retains a descending p and rounded 0. Two rightward bars survive at the main relation, while cancellation covers their left ends and curves through the lower relation, leaving = versus ≤ unresolved in both places.

Between the left sigma and its surviving n is a dense vertical zigzag cancellation extending below the formula baseline. A possible bowl and descending stroke are buried in it, so the proposed p cannot be isolated securely.

The subscript under the right sigma is one low horizontal stroke with a tiny upward entry at its left. The nearby n under the preceding sigma has a tall entry, raised arch and right downstroke; none of that arch structure appears in the target.

After the slanted notation text, an open angled stroke precedes a curved descending hook or loop. The underline passes immediately below, and the available strokes do not securely separate a question mark from a relation plus zero or establish a separate lower relation bar.

After Comme, the small word begins with an open cup and continues as a low joined stroke with a slight middle rise and falling end. The compressed tail does not securely separate a and s from n, and the initial cup lacks enough internal detail to decide c versus e.

The word before formules begins with a small oval and continues into a low thick tail; there is no distinct tall d ascender. The remaining strokes do not separately establish u and x or e and s, so the entire candidate choice remains uncertain.
The letter before =1 is an open cup with a long descending left stroke and shorter rising right stroke. It has no closed p bowl or raised n/m shoulders.

notes: Actual image dimensions are 1765 by 2608 source pixels. All row boxes use these unscaled coordinates, right and bottom excluded.
Every listed page mark boundary was read before assessing scope. No unmarked correction is claimed.
Primary report covers only M1431-M1439. M1439 is the canceled baseline layer, separate from M1440's raised rewrite.
The primary interval includes reading, tool operations and coordination; it is not continuous active-reading time.
Hard cases sent to coordinator: M1431, M1434, M1435 and M1439; word limitations for M1433 and M1437 were also communicated. No peer result has been incorporated in this initial report.

notes: Actual source dimensions measured as 1765 by 2608 pixels. Source page and all page MARKS.tsv boundaries were read; only assigned M1440–M1447 submitted.

Only Pillow crop, enlargement, contrast adjustment and rotation were used; every logged image was actually viewed. The primary interval includes communication and waiting between inspection phases, not continuous active reading.

M1441 is narrowed componentwise; the enclosing source deletion is preserved by replacing only the unsure span. M1440 is the literal first candidate and its supralinear replacement position is recorded in evidence without changing surrounding LaTeX.

Independent review requested through coordinator for difficult cancellation and margin strokes. M1443 peer agreement reported by coordinator did not substitute for the directly inspected adjacent n comparison.
